notes: The letter-by-letter wave reaches the end of the word now. Each letter was lit on the pacer clock and then made to wait a second time before it began to fade, so the tail of the wave was wiped when the line moved on and only the first letter ever looked lit.
A letter now carries only its own fade, sized from the window the word is really sung over, so a fast word sweeps across it instead of lighting as one soft block.

A song with a long instrumental opening is timed from the rise where the singing actually starts, not from the top of the file. The layout was pinned to a lead-in measured from zero, which pushed every later line further behind the voice.
The first line is snapped onto that rise like every other line. It used to be the one line the search never touched, so it stayed wherever the flat spread had put it.
The word-by-word highlight, the syllable weighting and the syllable pacing are unchanged in every other way, and the letter fade is the only thing the wrap sets.
The widget and the player are untouched: a press on the home-screen widget still resumes the song without opening the app.
